newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Records tumble in Europe after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Records tumble in Europe after U.S. data.

text.p: European financial markets pushed sharply higher across the board on Tuesday after U.S. economic data smoothed fears about inflation and rising interest rates.
U.S. treasury bonds immediately popped higher after the release of subdued consumer price index (CPI) and retail sales figures for December, and Wall Street followed suit.
Records tumbled across Europe as investors responded by pushing stock markets up on the belief that the American figures lowered the pressure on the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise rates.
The dollar zoomed to its highest point against the mark since July 1994, hitting 1.5973 marks. It also blipped up to 117.04 yen but was unable to hold above 117.
At least 10 European stock markets recorded record highs during the day, with most of them closing at a peak.

"The bond market is very strong, the dollar is rising sharply, the U.S. figures were in line with expectations -- all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds," said EIFB analyst Pierre Vignaud in Paris.
Although the French and British bourses set new highs during the morning, many investors played safe before the U.S. data.
In the event, core CPI figures for December were subdued and Christmas shopping boosted retail sales slightly more than expected.
Economists saw the figures showing that consumers had held spending in check, which should help to curb inflation and reduce pressure on interest rates.
"The CPI looks like a clear signal that things are on the right track and appears to have relaxed interest rate concerns," said Alan Ackerman, chief market strategist at Fahnestock & Co in New York.
Comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in Belgium earlier appeared to have little impact on markets.
Greenspan, who caused turmoil late last year by warning about irrational exuberance in financial markets, urged central banks not to take risks with inflation.
French stocks stormed to a powerful close, with the CAC-40 index ending at a record close of 2,402.14 for a rise of 1.73 percent. The CAC-40 futures contract rose 38.5 at 2,406.

Takeover and merger speculation excited trading in Cie Bancaire, a unit of Paribas bank, with shares in the finance house up 4.53 percent to 646 francs. Paribas's planned sale of Credit du Nord boosted its stock last week.
London shares posted strong gains for the second day in a row, as fears of an imminent rise in interest rates subsided on both sides of the Atlantic.

Led by surging bank and supermarket stocks, the FTSE 100 finished 60.9 points higher at a record 4,168.2. The rally has added 18.8 billion pounds ($31.44 billion) to blue-chip stocks over the last two sessions.
The FTSE surpassed its previous intraday peak of 4,123.2 set on New Year's Eve in its biggest one-day gain since November 22.
The gains were mainly due to growing hopes that interest rates would be left alone after Wednesday's monetary policy meeting between the government and Bank of England.
"People are no longer looking for a rate rise tomorrow," said one senior trader.
German shares, which were early laggards as investors held back, staged an afternoon surge with the IBIS DAX hitting a record 2,984.32 points in post-bourse electronic trading.
Although the IBIS DAX closed off its highs at 2,978, one German trader commented: "Unless there are any upsets from the U.S., I think we can reach the 3,000 points this week now."

Lufthansa fell 84 pfennigs to 21.01 marks but was well off its lows after aviation analysts suggested that draft laws designed to speed the airline's privatisation would not hit the holdings of international investors in practice.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5943 marks and 116.83 yen compared with 1.5890 and 116.30 late in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index closed up 60.9 points, or 1.48 percent, at 4,168.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index ended up 40.87 points, or 1.73 percent, at 2,402.14.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 6.07 points, at 2,948.88. In later electronic trading, the IBIS DAX ended up 22.06 points, or 0.75 percent, at 2,978.84.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $357.55 against $359.05 previously. Silver ended down a cent at $4.71.
